newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea shows no change in talks with U.S., South.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea shows no change in talks with U.S., South.

text.p: Officials from North and South Korea and the United States made no progress over Pyongyang's participation in proposed peace talks during a meeting on Sunday, a Seoul official said on Monday.
"Althouth North Korea called the unscheduled meeting, it showed no change in its earlier position," South Korea's foreign ministry spokesman told Reuters.
Pyongyang delegates twice failed to show up for high-level meetings last week scheduled to hear North Korea's reply to a proposal for four-nation peace talks, also including China.

The Sunday meeting was between North Korean chief delegate Kim Gye-gwan, his South Korean counterpart Song Young-shik and Mark Minton, who attened it on behalf of U.S. chief negotiator Charles Kartman, who was reported to be in Washington.
Foreign ministry spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung said a meeting including all delegates from the three countries was due to be held on Monday. "We will see what North Korea has to say in that meeting."

On Wednesday, Pyongyang essentially accepted the peace talks proposal but then tied acceptance to demands for additional food assistance, Lee said. Seoul and Washington say substantial food aid can be discussed after Pyongyang sits at the peace table.
